1473-Decision: `D-2026-09-21-scenario-execution-contract-amendment-1`. Amendment 1
1474-to `D-2026-09-21-scenario-execution-contract`. Six changes, accepted by the
1475-user on 2026-09-21 after reading
1476-`Docs/simulator-scenario-authoring-and-runtime.md`, which carries the full
1477-reasoning and is committed alongside this entry. The original decision keeps
1478-its ID and its unamended text; this entry is what it means where the two
1479-differ. The bracketed letters are the labels that document uses.
1480-
1481:**(c) Simultaneous causes are a group with a net effect, not a sequence.** The
1482-original decision fixed half-open dispatch and exactly-once application but
1483-left within-instant ordering unspecified, so two conforming kernels could
1484-legitimately disagree at that instant. Transitions on one state completing at
1485-the same offset now form a group with a net effect, and bounds are evaluated on
1486-the group's net rather than between its members. Order-dependence is decided
1487-exactly: apply all increases first to test the upper bound, all decreases first
1488-to test the lower. If neither extreme breaches, no ordering breaches, the net
1489-is unambiguous, and the contract answers. If one extreme breaches and the other
1490-does not, the group is genuinely order-dependent and the contract abstains with
1491-its own reason, saying the scenario must separate the offsets if it wants order
1492-to decide. Order is expressed as time, never as position in a document.
1493-
1494:A first draft of this rule declared authored `sequence` order and was reversed
1495-inside T019 before independent review. Authored order is not physics,
1496-serialising simultaneous causes abstains on a level the state is never in, and
1497-declaring it would have obliged T021's kernel to serialise sub-steps inside one
1498-instant, removing the metamorphic invariant
1499-`D-2026-09-21-causal-runtime-before-golden-traces` asks for. Already
1500-implemented on `task/T019-draft-run-setup` as a `DISPATCH_RULES` entry.
1501-
1502-**(d) `EXECUTION_CONTRACT_VERSION` moves when the space of conforming
1503-behaviours changes, including when it narrows, and never for wording.** Pinning
1504-a previously unspecified semantic narrows the space and moves the number; a
1505-prose edit does not. The number identifies the space, not the text. (c) moved
1506-it from 1 to 2 because it pinned an instant the first version left open, and
1507-rewriting (c)'s content inside the same slice did not move it again, because
1508-both drafts narrow the same space and no implementation ever conformed to the

1680-`foundation_binding`; a binding matching nothing; a binding matching more than

1682-a Foundation's answer is only locatable *through* the selected profile's

1689:the case that governs T020A's template-copy consequence, and the two must not
1690-be collapsed: *the profile's binding could not locate an answer* blocks, *the
1691-declared owner has no answer to locate* refuses.

1765-called, how narrow it is, or whether it emits a trajectory.

1967-Decision: `D-2026-09-22-expiry-follows-the-condition`. A thing that exists only
1968-because a condition holds names **the condition** as its expiry, never a slice
1969:number. Two artifacts in the M1C sequence exist for exactly that reason, they
1970-were each given a slice number, and in both cases the number was wrong.
1971-
1972-**The rule.** When something is created to cover a gap — a reference
1973-implementation standing in for a missing kernel, a disclosure standing in for a
1974-missing verifier — the thing that ends it is the condition closing, not a
1975-calendar position in a plan. A slice number is a guess about when the condition
1976-will close, and a guess written into a record is read later as a commitment.
1977-State the condition; let the slice that ends it be whichever slice ends it.

1980-is the part that separates the two instances and it is the useful half of the
1981-rule:
1982-

3888:Decision: `D-2026-10-09-s2-simulated-publication-clock`. Codex Architect, resolving S2-01c Planner Q1 in `.agent/architect-S2-01c-answers.md`. Select an explicitly advanced, persisted virtual publication clock for each registered Lab run. It is a simulated-device publication timeline, distinct from both the run's world-execution progress and the real UTC clock used for gateway diagnostics/server receipt. A world step may advance the publication clock through its reached simulation instant; after world execution completes, the operator/test harness may advance publication time further without rerunning the kernel. Pause and restart preserve the last advanced instant; neither wall-clock passage nor process restart releases a pending report. Advancing to an earlier instant refuses; repeated advancement to the same instant is idempotent.

3890:The Lab-private scheduler persists each delayed public reading, its original source instant, scheduled release instant, stable admission key and pending/released state before gateway submission. The scheduled instant is derived from the frozen delay window and remains private Lab scheduling provenance, not V3/Batch V2/GatewayDiagnostics data. At or after the due instant, the authenticated host advances the gateway's scoped per-run virtual publication clock and submits the unchanged public reading. The gateway owns and persists that clock and stamps `published_at` with its current virtual instant at first admission/sealing; if advancement skips past the scheduled instant, the actual virtual admission instant is used rather than backdating to the schedule. Require `published_at >= source_time`. Retry/restart reuse the same report key and stored envelope/batch bytes, never re-stamp or re-sequence. A pending report has no V3 envelope or sequence; it is visible in Lab as pending with source and scheduled instants. The gateway receives no private delay cause or oracle.

For SIMULATED evidence, `published_at - source_time` is a simulated reporting delay; `received_at - published_at` is not a physical transfer-lag measure when the clocks use different timelines. S2-02 must label these domains, display source/published/received instants with provenance and derive central diagnostic freshness from server receive time, not virtual Lab time. A future LIVE gateway uses its own real clock and does not inherit this Lab control.

3894:Decision: `D-2026-10-09-s2-gateway-diagnostic-semantics`. Codex Architect, resolving S2-01c phase-1 Q1-Q5 in `.agent/architect-S2-01c-answers-2.md`; this is a contract clarification, not an implementation review. Keep `GatewayDiagnosticsV1` pressure provenance off the V1 wire: `disk_pressure` is the gateway's operative `OK|WARN|STOP` level, while the local read identifies `MEASURED|INJECTED_FAULT_FIXTURE|UNMEASURABLE`. A simulated gateway's central STOP is not measured hardware pressure. At STOP, all new acquisition calls, including replays, refuse before writes or sequence allocation; sealing existing admitted envelopes and emitting diagnostics may continue. A failed free-space probe is locally `UNMEASURABLE` and operatively STOP. The default 60-second cadence and 1 GiB/256 MiB free-space WARN/STOP thresholds are frozen, provisioned demo values, not universal physical safety limits.

3896-Persist at most one immutable diagnostic per declared real-UTC cadence slot; a repeat returns its exact stored identity and bytes, and a clock earlier than the latest slot refuses. State changes within a slot are visible in the local read immediately but reach the wire in the next slot; the server uses receive time and cadence to decide central freshness. `queue_count` is the number of `STAGED|READY|IN_FLIGHT` envelopes, sealed or unbatched, excluding holds and dead letters; queue age uses their real-UTC outbox creation time and must remain real UTC when Lab V3 `published_at` becomes virtual. The local read retains sealed/unbatched/held/refused/dead-letter breakdown. `mapping_error_count` is the number of distinct `mapping_hold` rows with kind in `{NO_ACTIVE_MAPPING, UNKNOWN_CHANNEL, SOURCE_NOT_PERMITTED, OUTSIDE_VALIDITY, UNIT_INCOMPATIBLE, INVALID_ENUM}`; it is not the total held-report count. Contact is gateway real-UTC observation of a public report that resolves to a permitted source, even on replay or later hold; never-heard remains null. For a SIMULATED gateway its provenance is `OBSERVED_SIMULATED_REPORT`, never proof of physical controller contact or source health. S2-02 carries these meanings into authenticated receipt and central presentation without adding cause or private Lab fields to V1.

## Question 1: the sequence-order deviation

**Is the change fixture forcing?** No, in the sense N5 guards against. N5 forbids changing the fixture to make
Leg A's precondition hold. Leg A and N5 pass identically under both numberings, and I reproduced both. The change
affects only the S3/S4 re-evaluation in Leg B, which is upstream reviewed code, not this slice. The packet's phase 3
row says only "one mean withheld until a later decided time", so it fixes no numbering. Run 1 is recorded
transparently. Under SOURCE_ORDER, the variant models a reading the gateway sequenced on time whose upload arrived
late. That is a legitimate path, since sealed batches may upload independently (S2-02). I accept it as authoring.

**But the stated rationale is wrong for this repository, and the real-path consequence is understated (F1).**

## Findings

### F1 (Medium, residual risk and Architect question; not an S4-02c acceptance gap): this project's own late-reading path produces run 1, and run 1 yields current S5-eligible money that is understated without saying so

Files:
- `backend/conversions/s4-power-late-demo-cases-v1.json:11` (`sequence_rule`);
- `.agent/S4-02c-walkthrough-evidence.md` "Run 1";
- packet "Residual risk: New (from run 1)";
- `.ai/CODE_STATE.md` ("late-delivery sequence numbering on real gateways unproved").

The fixture says "a store-and-forward gateway numbers readings when it takes them", so the late mean fills its gap.
That holds only when the gateway *takes* the reading on time and the upload is late. In this repository, the
gateway allocates the next sequence at admission (`gateway/assetops_gateway/service.py:9-11`: "read/increment
sequence" inside the admission transaction). Under `D-2026-10-09-s2-simulated-publication-clock`, a Lab-delayed
reading "has no V3 envelope or sequence" until it is released. So the Lab's simulated late delivery, and any device
reading that reaches the gateway late, takes a sequence *after* later readings: exactly run 1's numbering. The
packet calls this "not proved here". It is determinable from the code, and it is the default late path for S2-S7
simulated input.

What run 1 actually does (my reproduction, then dropped):
- S3 marks `SEQUENCE_ORDER_INVERTED: generator_power 07:05..08:00`. The **window** assessment is `INDETERMINATE`
  with `GENERATOR_SERIES_AMBIGUOUS`.
- The revised **FindingRevision** r2 nonetheless stays `SUPPORTED`/`CANDIDATE_AVOIDABLE`, and its episode shrinks
  to `[06:05, 07:00)`:
  - candidate minutes fall from 115 to 55, and indeterminate minutes stay 0;
  - its only limitation is `OPEN_BOUND: no OFF evidence after the interval`. That misattributes the end of the
    interval, which ends because of the series refusal, not because of missing OFF evidence.
- Its consequence drains to **CURRENT PRICED, 7.5625 USD over 11 means**, and the money predicate the tool uses
  (CURRENT, PRICED, amount present) makes it **S5-eligible**. That is less than half of the 15.8125 USD the same
  physical data gives when numbered in source order. Neither the Finding nor the consequence names the inversion.

So the answer to "can a real late reading never yield current money via this path?" is: **it does yield current
money, but understated, and the truncation is silent at the Finding and consequence level.** The packet has the
direction of the risk the wrong way round. The risk is not that money never arrives. It is that money which is too
low arrives as current.

Effect on acceptance:
- **S4-02c:** none. Item 3/5 and Leg A behave identically. The consequence correctly derives from r2's accepted
  inputs, and the S3 cohort rule and the Finding episode limitation are S3-01/S4-01 reviewed behaviour.
- **S5-01 and real-Site readiness:** affected. S5-01's money read (`mini:4#a`) would show this figure as current.

Fix on the branch (Low, documentation): scope the `sequence_rule` text and the evidence or packet residual-risk
wording to "a reading sequenced on time and uploaded late". State that admission-time sequencing (Lab-delayed or
device-late readings) gives run 1, with the measured result above. Do not change the fixture again.

Architect questions (batch them, per the owner's routing):
- **Q1.** Should S3's cohort rule (`backend/assetops_backend/analytics/cohort.py` `series_limits`, docstring lines
  17-20) treat a gateway-admission-sequenced late reading as an inversion? The technical design says "monotonic
  arrival is not required" (technical design, V3 identity paragraph) and that "late or out-of-order evidence
  recomputes the affected and neighboring continuity window" (Assess step 4). Today the rule refuses the whole
  later span.
- **Q2.** When the window is `INDETERMINATE` with `GENERATOR_SERIES_AMBIGUOUS` over part of a Finding's former
  episode, must the revised FindingRevision carry that limitation (rather than only `OPEN_BOUND`)? And must the S5
  money predicate exclude, or label, a consequence whose FindingRevision's window is INDETERMINATE?
- **Q3.** Does this belong with `R1` and the owner's analysis-input backlog item ("analysis input data for
  simulated and real Sites"), or as its own node ahead of S5-01?

### F2 (Low, tool regression in strictness): the S4-02b `recompute` no longer fails when a work item fails

`tools/s402b_fuel_cost_walkthrough.py:169-182`. Before M1, `tree_py(..., check=True)` raised on the runner's exit 1
(any item failed). Now exit 1 is tolerated, failed items are printed, and the function returns normally, so the tool
exits 0. The new `.mjs` claims (`tools/s402b-fuel-cost-evidence.mjs:254-255`) check that exit status and would
therefore pass with failed items. The later API claims would probably still catch a bad amount, but the
"recompute succeeded" claim no longer means what it says. In the same loop, if 50 runs exhaust with backlog left,
the tool also exits silently.

Fix: after printing, `raise SystemExit(1)` when `failed` is non-empty or the loop ended with backlog > 0.

### F3 (Info, housekeeping): earlier-phase scratch databases remain on the shared server

`assetops_s402c_mut_test`, `assetops_s402c_p1_test`, `assetops_s402c2_main_test`, `assetops_s402c2_mut_test`,
`assetops_s402c2_full_test`. None is phase 3's: the phase 3 `s402c3*` databases were dropped, as were all of mine.
They are worth dropping before merge.

### Not findings (checked)

- **N5:** a real assertion. `walk()` stops unless `[07:00, 07:05)` lies inside the merged observed Candidate
  spans, and it also requires the reason to be anything other than `CANDIDATE_SPAN_UNVERIFIED`
  (`tools/s402c_late_power_walkthrough.py:243-250`). Pre-late result: `POWER_COVERAGE_GAP`.
- **N7 / the phase 3 row "include unrelated accepted input as typed no-op":** not shown by the fixture (one bound
  generator), stated in the evidence, and proved in `test_s4_evidence_drain_postgres.py`. The plan re-review
  explicitly allowed this.
- **C5:** exact work, attempt, consequence, accepted and examined IDs and digests are in the evidence JSON. My
  run's IDs differ (fresh DB) and its pattern matches.
- **The superseded no-op branch** did not arise because evidence work drained before r2 existed. The packet says
  so, and the Postgres test covers it.
- **Reads with `source_open=True`:** an honest, stated deviation. The source gate is S4-02b's, and it is exercised

## Outcome and authority

A genuinely accepted late generator-power mean that can alter an existing Site FindingRevision's `fuel-cost-1` technical input creates durable consequence work atomically with acceptance. Before drain, the old consequence is `STALE/TECHNICAL_INPUT_CHANGED` (or `PENDING` without a head) with a real queued work ID. Draining that **same** FindingRevision yields a current `QUANTITY_UNAVAILABLE/POWER_NOT_IN_ASSESSMENT_INPUTS` revision: the late reading was not an input to its cited analytic run. S3 `process-jobs` and S4 `match-findings` must re-evaluate the Finding and append a revised FindingRevision before a new `CURRENT/PRICED` consequence can become S5-01 eligible. All revisions remain inspectable. A stale read alone does not complete this slice.

Drop `financial_consequence_work_finding_revision_once`; replace it with a partial unique index on `(finding_revision_id) WHERE cause = 'FINDING_REVISION_APPENDED'`. `CREATE OR REPLACE FUNCTION financial_consequence_dirty_on_finding_revision()` with `ON CONFLICT (finding_revision_id) WHERE cause = 'FINDING_REVISION_APPENDED' DO NOTHING`. Keep assumption uniqueness. Add a partial unique index on `(accepted_evidence_id, finding_revision_id) WHERE cause = 'EVIDENCE_ACCEPTED'`. Replace `financial_consequence_work_cause_shape` with an explicit three-arm CHECK: assumption has only assumption locator; Finding append has only Finding locator; evidence has exact accepted ID plus Finding and revision locators, with other cause locators null. Preserve range and scope checks; index pending selection by tenant/Site and attempt lookup by `(work_id, attempt_no DESC)`. It never deletes append-only evidence or work.
21-2. **Transactional enqueue.** Migration 0012 adds an `AFTER INSERT` trigger on `ingestion_disposition` for `decision = 'ACCEPTED'`, joined to its stored `accepted_evidence_id`. It runs inside `decide_chunk` only for a genuine accepted disposition; duplicate, conflict, rejection and exact replay do not enqueue. Filter on the stored, binding-derived `accepted_evidence.role = 'generator_power'`, never a client role. Select existing tenant/Site Findings by strict half-open overlap with their latest revision's episode; zero-width episodes do not overlap. Here and in the worker, **latest eligible FindingRevision** means the Finding's highest `revision_no` in the same tenant/Site; lifecycle/source gating is left to `quantify` and the read, not the selector. Insert one row per accepted ID and selected revision using the evidence partial unique index. Coarse selection may no-op later but must not omit a possibly affected Finding. Trigger failure rolls back acceptance and disposition. Retain the 0011 FindingRevision-insert trigger so new/revised Findings enqueue independently. Before either trigger selects/inserts work, both take the same transaction-scoped Site advisory lock keyed by `financial_consequence_enqueue:` plus `site_id`. At READ COMMITTED, select after acquiring the lock so acceptance racing a FindingRevision append cannot miss its committed revision. Prove with two Postgres connections. Rule 8 remains unchanged: no Python module inserts `financial_consequence_work`.
22-3. **Scoped drain.** Explicitly dispatch all three causes; an unknown cause records a typed failure (or is skipped) and never falls through to assumption-range recompute, including if phase 1 deploys before phase 2. If queued revision has been superseded, record a typed successful no-op for its work row; the new revision's 0011 insert work derives its consequence. Irrelevant role, asset or window also no-ops without consequence append. A transiently missing/closed source records a typed FAILED attempt and remains retryable; wrong-Site scope fails without fallback. Derive only from that revision's accepted public analytic inputs. The same-revision late reading becomes `QUANTITY_UNAVAILABLE/POWER_NOT_IN_ASSESSMENT_INPUTS` after drain; never substitute it into the old analytic input set. Existing basis uniqueness and per-revision append lock return the existing consequence ID on unchanged/repeated work, concurrent runs and append-then-crash retry. A work item succeeds only when every selected target appended, replayed or no-opped.
23:4. **Run plan and retry.** Extend the server-side CLI as a **one-shot** bounded `run --tenant ... --site ... --limit N` under an external one-minute timer (document a Windows Task Scheduler or systemd timer invocation, owner, cadence and recovery). frontend/docs/architecture/production-shaped-mvp-technical-design.md:43:`gateway_diagnostic` is the central operational-health table, separate from `accepted_evidence`: `id`, `tenant_id`, `site_id`, `gateway_id`, `sequence_epoch`, `diagnostic_sequence`, `observed_at`, `received_at`, `last_device_contact_by_source jsonb`, `queue_count`, `oldest_queue_age_seconds?`, `disk_pressure`, `clock_offset_ms?`, `mapping_error_count`, `payload_sha256`. Same identity/hash is an idempotent retry; changed bytes with the same identity are refused and audited. Rows are append-only. The server, not the gateway clock, sets `received_at` and computes current contact freshness from a declared heartbeat cadence. A stale/missing report never becomes a healthy-device assertion. This table and `GatewayDiagnosticsV1` are the recorded `A-edge-diagnostics` contract; S2-01c/S2-02 refine cadence and limits.

frontend/docs/architecture/production-shaped-mvp-technical-design.md-74-## 2. Edge SQLite schema
frontend/docs/architecture/production-shaped-mvp-technical-design.md-75-
frontend/docs/architecture/production-shaped-mvp-technical-design.md:76:Use `PRAGMA journal_mode=WAL`, `foreign_keys=ON`, `busy_timeout`, one writer, and a migration table. SQLite is an acquisition ledger, not a product database. Store UTC instants as ISO text. A source stream means `(gateway_id,source_id)`; `sequence_epoch` changes only on explicit reprovisioning, preventing accidental sequence reuse after restore. Local primary keys can be text UUIDs. Example values below correspond to the central examples.

frontend/docs/architecture/production-shaped-mvp-technical-design.md-89-
frontend/docs/architecture/production-shaped-mvp-technical-design.md:90:**Crash sequence:** device report → map/validate → `BEGIN IMMEDIATE` → read/increment sequence → derive message ID from `(site,gateway,source,epoch,sequence)` → insert canonical envelope and bytes → commit → select READY rows and seal homogeneous batch in a second transaction → POST → verify receipt digest/IDs/count → persist ack and state in one transaction. On restart, reset `IN_FLIGHT` batches to retryable; never recreate a sealed payload. `ACKED` may be compacted after configured retention and backed-up receipt checkpoint; `DEAD_LETTER` and unacknowledged rows remain. Disk pressure stops acquisition visibly rather than dropping evidence silently. If a device provides a durable event ID, store it in the report metadata and use it for duplicate suppression **before** sequence assignment; otherwise repeated physical samples are distinct events and never silently conflated.

frontend/docs/architecture/production-shaped-mvp-technical-design.md-130-
frontend/docs/architecture/production-shaped-mvp-technical-design.md:131:The existing v1/v2 envelope and v1 batch parser remain read-compatible for stored demo history. V3 **changes identity semantics**: `message_id = SHA256(length-delimited(site_id,gateway_id,source_id,sequence_epoch,sequence))`, with the tuple durably allocated once. Exact byte framing and test vectors are part of the contract task; do not concatenate without separators or trust a sender-supplied digest. Sequence scope is `(gateway,source,epoch)`; monotonic arrival is not required. `published_at` is when gateway seals publication, not a second measurement time. Source clock uncertainty is expressed as quality/diagnostic metadata, never correction of `source_time`. Batch V2 is homogeneous in source/mapping/Foundation reference; each envelope is still checked against effective configuration at its own time. The batch hash is over canonical bytes excluding the `payload_sha256` field; the receipt hash similarly excludes `receipt_sha256`. Batch `source_mode` is compared with authenticated gateway registration and is only provenance after that check. Wire IDs for site/gateway/source resolve registered UUID rows; device/signal IDs remain scoped source strings. A production batch must not carry Lab-private cause or truth; keep any Lab run reference in a private manifest keyed by batch ID.
frontend/docs/architecture/production-shaped-mvp-technical-design.md-132-
frontend/docs/architecture/production-shaped-mvp-technical-design.md-133-`GatewayDiagnosticsV1` is sent independently of observations so an idle or disconnected source can still report gateway state. Its hash uses canonical bytes excluding `payload_sha256`; the registered gateway credential scopes the POST. It never enters `AcceptedEvidence` or analytic input sets. For the S2 demo, Batch V2 uses registered TLS gateway authentication, canonical SHA-256 and exact-byte retries; per-batch cryptographic signing/key rotation are deferred. A later decision to sign must amend this contract and its canonical test vectors before implementation.

frontend/docs/architecture/production-shaped-mvp-technical-design.md:173:`QueryScope.window` is half-open `[start,end)` and required for analytic/product queries. `knowledge_at` makes historical audits reproducible; normal UI defaults to current server time. `selected_revision_id` freezes a drill-down even if the surrounding window changes. `AnalyticInputSet.input_sha256` hashes sorted evidence IDs **and their content digests**, resolved configuration/binding revisions, window, analytic/model version and canonical role coverage. frontend/docs/architecture/production-shaped-mvp-technical-design.md-174-
frontend/docs/architecture/production-shaped-mvp-technical-design.md-175-## 4. Transaction and processing contracts
frontend/docs/architecture/production-shaped-mvp-technical-design.md-176-
frontend/docs/architecture/production-shaped-mvp-technical-design.md-177-1. **Register configuration.** Publish Foundation and SignalBinding versions together under Site lock. Validate site type, role vocabulary, units, asset ownership and non-overlapping current valid periods. Persist canonical snapshot hash for authenticated gateway download; no detached snapshot signature or key-rotation system is required in S1–S7. Backdated publication enqueues affected windows for recomputation; do not change accepted evidence bytes.
frontend/docs/architecture/production-shaped-mvp-technical-design.md-178-2. **Receive batch.** TLS and gateway credential establish tenant/site/gateway/source. Enforce size/count limits before parsing; resolve external batch ID and digest. Identical retry returns stored receipt; conflicting retry records/refuses without touching prior decisions. A batch with wrong registered mode or configuration reference is refused as a whole.
frontend/docs/architecture/production-shaped-mvp-technical-design.md:179:3. **Decide records.** In one Postgres transaction, lock batch row; for each unprocessed ordinal parse strict envelope, verify identity/sequence and referenced mapping/Foundation validity at `source_time`, normalize with the registered as-accepted conversion, and insert acceptance or rejection plus disposition. Unique message key arbitrates concurrent duplicate deliveries. Equal digest is `DUPLICATE`; changed digest is `CONFLICT` and points to first accepted evidence. Update watermark and create/coalesce recompute jobs in the same commit. Chunk a large batch into short committed transactions; receipt exposes `IN_PROGRESS` until all ordinals are durable. A client retries the same batch/bytes and resumes from the persisted watermark. Return a terminal receipt only after all decisions commit.
frontend/docs/architecture/production-shaped-mvp-technical-design.md:180:4. **Assess.** Worker leases dirty site/domain/window jobs, selects accepted evidence by source time plus interval overlap at a declared knowledge cutoff, resolves the exact public configuration, builds `AnalyticInputSet`, and runs the versioned pure analytic. In one commit insert `AnalyticRun`, immutable assessment/finding/consequence revisions when basis changed, update projections and mark job done. Retry of same input hash is a no-op. Late or out-of-order evidence recomputes the affected and neighboring continuity window; it never mutates old revisions. Model deployment schedules explicit re-evaluation of supported windows.
frontend/docs/architecture/production-shaped-mvp-technical-design.md-181-5. **Verify.** ActionEvent records work. After a later closed window exists, evaluate the frozen plan against accepted evidence, target and each guardrail. Missing coverage is `INCONCLUSIVE`; worsening service prevents `VERIFIED` even if cost falls. Link outcome to exact analytic run/evidence and surface any later superseding outcome.
frontend/docs/architecture/production-shaped-mvp-technical-design.md-182-
frontend/docs/architecture/production-shaped-mvp-technical-design.md-183-**Initial API contract:** `POST /api/ingestion/batches` returns terminal `200` receipt or `202 IN_PROGRESS` receipt; `GET /api/ingestion/batches/{id}` returns the same durable state. `409` is reserved for same batch ID/different bytes or registered identity conflict, `422` for malformed contract, `401/403` for authentication/authorization. Normal reads use `GET /api/sites/{id}/evidence`, `/evidence/records/{id}`, `/overview`, `/performance/{view}`, `/findings/{id}` with `from`, `to` and optional `revision_id`; list reads paginate by stable `(source_time,id)` or `(created_at,id)` cursor. All responses include scope/window, revision IDs, evidence coverage and projection watermark. The UI treats a lagging projection as pending, not healthy. Lab Commit calls this same HTTP boundary with a registered simulated gateway; no privileged product-write endpoint exists.

frontend/docs/architecture/production-shaped-mvp-technical-design.md-186-
frontend/docs/architecture/production-shaped-mvp-technical-design.md-187-**Demo-to-Postgres cutover:** create Tenant/Site/Gateway/Source registrations from existing Site records, import immutable Foundation and mapping versions, then replay sealed committed batch bytes through the new ingestion service using the legacy parsers. Preserve original batch/message IDs, envelope text, source times and mode; assign new database UUIDs only to internal rows. Compare accepted/rejected/conflict counts and representative evidence/dispatch claims against the file-backed baseline. Keep `var/sites`, Lab runs, stages and committed artifacts untouched and read-only during verification. Switch product reads to Postgres only after the comparison passes; new Lab Commit posts the V2 batch/receipt path. Do not import private world trajectories into the product database. An existing batch whose required public configuration cannot be registered is reported as a migration exception, never guessed into a new Foundation version.

frontend/docs/architecture/production-shaped-mvp-technical-design.md:189:**Acceptance checks for the first slices:** power loss after SQLite enqueue and after server commit; duplicate batch with identical bytes; same ID with different bytes; partial batch crash/retry; reordered and late samples; two same-timestamp samples with different sequences; mapping/Foundation version change during offline period; wrong gateway/site credential; one rejected sibling among valid samples; central diagnostic receipt/reload and stale-heartbeat behavior. Before drain, the old consequence is `STALE/TECHNICAL_INPUT_CHANGED` (or `PENDING` without a head) with a real queued work ID. S3 `process-jobs` and S4 `match-findings` must re-evaluate the Finding and append a revised FindingRevision before a new `CURRENT/PRICED` consequence can become S5-01 eligible. All revisions remain inspectable. A stale read alone does not complete this slice.

19-
20-1. **Migration 0012 and constraints.** Add `EVIDENCE_ACCEPTED` and a tenant/Site-scoped FK to exact `accepted_evidence.id` on `financial_consequence_work`. An evidence row records accepted ID, Finding ID, selected FindingRevision ID and half-open affected interval. Drop `financial_consequence_work_finding_revision_once`; replace it with a partial unique index on `(finding_revision_id) WHERE cause = 'FINDING_REVISION_APPENDED'`. `CREATE OR REPLACE FUNCTION financial_consequence_dirty_on_finding_revision()` with `ON CONFLICT (finding_revision_id) WHERE cause = 'FINDING_REVISION_APPENDED' DO NOTHING`. Replace `financial_consequence_work_cause_shape` with an explicit three-arm CHECK: assumption has only assumption locator; Finding append has only Finding locator; evidence has exact accepted ID plus Finding and revision locators, with other cause locators null. +# Architect rulings: S4-02c review F1 Q1–Q3 and R1 (2026-10-14)
+
+Inputs: `.agent/S4-02c-review.md` F1 and registry closeout notes, `.agent/S4-02c-review-packet.md`, `.agent/S4-02c-walkthrough-evidence.md` run 1, `tasks/S4-02c-evidence-consequence-work.md` R1; `D-2026-10-09-s2-simulated-publication-clock`, the S3 dispatch decisions, `D-2026-10-14-s402-post-review-follow-ons`, and `D-2026-10-14-s5-selected-window-overview`. This is a ruling for subsequent work, not a change to S4-02c's reviewed contract.
+
+## Q1 — sequence and source time
+
+**Rule:** An admission-allocated gateway sequence is transport/admission order, not proof of source-time order. For a registered same-source, same-epoch stream whose source-time/interval semantics and clock quality are attested and valid, S3 must place readings by source time. A later gateway sequence with an earlier source time is a late arrival, not `SEQUENCE_ORDER_INVERTED` by itself. Preserve duplicate, overlap, conflicting epoch, untrusted clock, and impossible-time refusals; where the source-time basis cannot be established, report a named series limit rather than silently sort and claim coherence. This does not bless arbitrary backdating. The Lab-delayed publication clock supplies a deterministic case: the withheld report has no sequence before release, so admission numbering naturally runs backward against source time.
+
+**Owner and timing:** S3 cohort/assessment (`dispatch-3.x`) plus S2 gateway/publication-profile proof, in `I-late-reading-series-and-money-limit`, **before S5-01's money read and before a real-Site pilot**. Changing the reviewed cohort rule requires a new model version, reassessment/reconciliation of affected current windows and preservation of old `dispatch-3.1` revisions and exact links as history. The implementer must prove both on-time-sequenced late upload and admission-sequenced delayed admission through accepted public evidence. A real gateway without validated source-time/clock semantics stays limited.
+
+## Q2 — Finding limit and money
+
+**Rule:** A revised Finding must carry the selected assessment's material `GENERATOR_SERIES_AMBIGUOUS`/`SEQUENCE_ORDER_INVERTED` limit when it removes or truncates the prior candidate episode. Its end reason must identify the series refusal; `OPEN_BOUND` alone is false for the run-1 truncation. Preserve the supported `[06:05, 07:00)` portion if its exact evidence remains coherent, but disclose that the later portion is unassessed, not disproved or repaired. S4 owns FindingRevision propagation and its read/UI; a changed claim basis appends a revision.
+
+S5's `mini:4#a` money read **withholds the amount** if generator-series ambiguity affects the selected Finding/window, even if a narrower consequence is `CURRENT PRICED`. Show an explicit no-current-amount state with the assessment/Finding limit and exact links. This is a fail-closed rule for the demonstrated silent understatement, not a claim that every `INDETERMINATE` window has no valid candidate time. Once S3 resolves and reassesses that series under a reviewed rule, S5 may show a same-basis current amount for the proven Candidate span, with any remaining material limits visible. S4 consequence currentness remains a statement about the cited FindingRevision's technical/price basis; S5 eligibility is a stricter presentation gate. Do not rewrite historical $7.5625 or $15.8125 consequences.
+
+**Owner and timing:** S4 Finding projection and S5 `I-site-overview-read`/UI consume the S3 decision in `I-late-reading-series-and-money-limit`; **before S5-01**. The real-Site pilot also needs the source-time/clock proof. A regression must replay run 1 and the source-ordered variant and assert the assessment status, Finding limitations/end reason, consequence lineage and S5 amount eligibility; the 7.5625 USD current consequence must never become an unqualified current Overview amount.
+
+## Q3 — placement and gates
+
+**Rule:** F1 gets its own sized node, `I-late-reading-series-and-money-limit` (**M**), because it changes reviewed S3 assessment semantics, S4 claim semantics and S5 money eligibility. It is a hard prerequisite of `I-site-overview-read`, hence S5-01, with `I-S2-02`, `I-S3-01`, `I-S4-01`, `I-S4-02b` as inputs. The node's acceptance target records both late-numbering variants and the no-silent-money result. It also gates the first real-Site pilot. The owner's “analysis input data for simulated and real Sites” backlog item remains the broader W1-exit contract for per-analytic required inputs, cadence and coverage; it should include source-time/clock attestation at that review, but does not substitute for this narrower S5 defect gate. R1 concerns operating the already defined jobs and is separate from semantic correctness.
+
+## R1 — run the S3 and S4 workers
+
+**Rule:** Create `I-analytic-finding-worker-schedule` (**S**), requiring S3, S4 and S4-02c's consequence-work node, and gate `I-site-overview-read` on it. Install or explicitly configure an environment-owned bounded schedule for `process-jobs` then `match-findings` across active tenant/Sites; report backlog, last success/failure, retry and stopped-worker conditions. Keep S5 `PENDING`/`STALE_PROJECTION` while upstream work is outstanding. A late accepted reading must reach a revised Finding and consequence without the manual Leg B commands. The S4-02c one-shot consequence runner and its documented external timer do not schedule S3/S4.
+
+**Owner and timing:** S3/S4 worker operation, with S5 currentness integration; **before S5-01**, and therefore before W1 exit or a real-Site pilot that claims automatic late-evidence recovery. The Planner should refine deployment ownership and cadence in a small follow-on packet. No new scheduler mechanism is mandated if an existing reliable environment timer can meet the acceptance target.
+
+## Acceptance and owner decision
+
+S4-02c remains **accepted with carries**. Its transactional enqueue, scoped drain, one-shot run plan and two-leg authored demonstration satisfy its packet. F1 is upstream S3/S4 semantics and a new S5 eligibility requirement; R1 is unscheduled upstream operations. The reviewer explicitly did not make either an S4-02c acceptance gap. Close `I-evidence-acceptance-consequence-work` on merge after the review's documentation carries; leave the two new nodes open.
+
+**Owner input:** No additional product choice is needed to make these safety and lineage rulings. The owner should see the no-amount state and limited Finding at the existing S5-01 visual checkpoint, and decide any broader analysis-input policy at the W1-exit review. If the owner wants partial, explicitly limited money from an indeterminate generator series, that would be a new product/risk decision with a separate reviewed contract; it is not implied by the current S5 eligibility rule.
+
+## Draft DECISIONS entry
+
+Decision: `D-2026-10-14-s402c-late-sequence-and-s5-money`. The Architect rules that gateway admission sequence does not establish source-time order for a validated store-and-forward source. S3 must version a source-time-aware cohort rule with explicit clock/overlap/epoch limits and reassess affected windows without rewriting history. S4 must carry a material series refusal into the revised Finding and state why the episode ends. Until a reviewed reassessment resolves generator-series ambiguity, S5 withholds an amount for that affected selected Finding/window despite a `CURRENT PRICED` consequence, and shows the limitation and exact lineage. `I-late-reading-series-and-money-limit` and `I-analytic-finding-worker-schedule` are separate prerequisites of `I-site-overview-read` before S5-01; both also gate real-Site readiness. The latter schedules S3/S4 workers and makes backlog/failure visible so late evidence reaches the revised Finding without manual commands. The broader simulated/real analysis-input backlog remains for W1 exit. S4-02c acceptance is unchanged; its reviewed consequence work may close on merge. The S5 owner visual checkpoint remains required.
+
+## Plain-language owner summary
+
+The gateway numbers a delayed reading when it arrives. Today that can make the analysis stop early and show **$7.5625 as current** where the same readings numbered in their source order yield **$15.8125**, without saying the series was cut short. I have gated the S5 money card until the reading order is handled under a reviewed rule and the Finding explains any remaining limit. I also added a small scheduling gate so delayed evidence reaches the revised analysis and Finding automatically. This does not reopen S4-02c's acceptance.

+# Architect rulings: S4-02c review F1 Q1–Q3 and R1 (2026-10-14)
+
+Inputs: `.agent/S4-02c-review.md` F1 and registry closeout notes, `.agent/S4-02c-review-packet.md`, `.agent/S4-02c-walkthrough-evidence.md` run 1, `tasks/S4-02c-evidence-consequence-work.md` R1; `D-2026-10-09-s2-simulated-publication-clock`, the S3 dispatch decisions, `D-2026-10-14-s402-post-review-follow-ons`, and `D-2026-10-14-s5-selected-window-overview`. This is a ruling for subsequent work, not a change to S4-02c's reviewed contract.
+
+## Q1 — sequence and source time
+
+**Rule:** An admission-allocated gateway sequence is transport/admission order, not proof of source-time order. For a registered same-source, same-epoch stream whose source-time/interval semantics and clock quality are attested and valid, S3 must place readings by source time. A later gateway sequence with an earlier source time is a late arrival, not `SEQUENCE_ORDER_INVERTED` by itself. Preserve duplicate, overlap, conflicting epoch, untrusted clock, and impossible-time refusals; where the source-time basis cannot be established, report a named series limit rather than silently sort and claim coherence. This does not bless arbitrary backdating. The Lab-delayed publication clock supplies a deterministic case: the withheld report has no sequence before release, so admission numbering naturally runs backward against source time.
+
+**Owner and timing:** S3 cohort/assessment (`dispatch-3.x`) plus S2 gateway/publication-profile proof, in `I-late-reading-series-and-money-limit`, **before S5-01's money read and before a real-Site pilot**. Changing the reviewed cohort rule requires a new model version, reassessment/reconciliation of affected current windows and preservation of old `dispatch-3.1` revisions and exact links as history. The implementer must prove both on-time-sequenced late upload and admission-sequenced delayed admission through accepted public evidence. A real gateway without validated source-time/clock semantics stays limited.
+
+## Q2 — Finding limit and money
+
+**Rule:** A revised Finding must carry the selected assessment's material `GENERATOR_SERIES_AMBIGUOUS`/`SEQUENCE_ORDER_INVERTED` limit when it removes or truncates the prior candidate episode. Its end reason must identify the series refusal; `OPEN_BOUND` alone is false for the run-1 truncation. Preserve the supported `[06:05, 07:00)` portion if its exact evidence remains coherent, but disclose that the later portion is unassessed, not disproved or repaired. S4 owns FindingRevision propagation and its read/UI; a changed claim basis appends a revision.
+
+S5's `mini:4#a` money read **withholds the amount** if generator-series ambiguity affects the selected Finding/window, even if a narrower consequence is `CURRENT PRICED`. Show an explicit no-current-amount state with the assessment/Finding limit and exact links. This is a fail-closed rule for the demonstrated silent understatement, not a claim that every `INDETERMINATE` window has no valid candidate time. Once S3 resolves and reassesses that series under a reviewed rule, S5 may show a same-basis current amount for the proven Candidate span, with any remaining material limits visible. S4 consequence currentness remains a statement about the cited FindingRevision's technical/price basis; S5 eligibility is a stricter presentation gate. Do not rewrite historical $7.5625 or $15.8125 consequences.
+
+**Owner and timing:** S4 Finding projection and S5 `I-site-overview-read`/UI consume the S3 decision in `I-late-reading-series-and-money-limit`; **before S5-01**. The real-Site pilot also needs the source-time/clock proof. A regression must replay run 1 and the source-ordered variant and assert the assessment status, Finding limitations/end reason, consequence lineage and S5 amount eligibility; the 7.5625 USD current consequence must never become an unqualified current Overview amount.
+
+## Q3 — placement and gates
+
+**Rule:** F1 gets its own sized node, `I-late-reading-series-and-money-limit` (**M**), because it changes reviewed S3 assessment semantics, S4 claim semantics and S5 money eligibility. It is a hard prerequisite of `I-site-overview-read`, hence S5-01, with `I-S2-02`, `I-S3-01`, `I-S4-01`, `I-S4-02b` as inputs. The node's acceptance target records both late-numbering variants and the no-silent-money result. It also gates the first real-Site pilot. The owner's “analysis input data for simulated and real Sites” backlog item remains the broader W1-exit contract for per-analytic required inputs, cadence and coverage; it should include source-time/clock attestation at that review, but does not substitute for this narrower S5 defect gate. R1 concerns operating the already defined jobs and is separate from semantic correctness.
+
+## R1 — run the S3 and S4 workers
+
+**Rule:** Create `I-analytic-finding-worker-schedule` (**S**), requiring S3, S4 and S4-02c's consequence-work node, and gate `I-site-overview-read` on it. Install or explicitly configure an environment-owned bounded schedule for `process-jobs` then `match-findings` across active tenant/Sites; report backlog, last success/failure, retry and stopped-worker conditions. Keep S5 `PENDING`/`STALE_PROJECTION` while upstream work is outstanding. A late accepted reading must reach a revised Finding and consequence without the manual Leg B commands. The S4-02c one-shot consequence runner and its documented external timer do not schedule S3/S4.
+
+**Owner and timing:** S3/S4 worker operation, with S5 currentness integration; **before S5-01**, and therefore before W1 exit or a real-Site pilot that claims automatic late-evidence recovery. The Planner should refine deployment ownership and cadence in a small follow-on packet. No new scheduler mechanism is mandated if an existing reliable environment timer can meet the acceptance target.
+
+## Acceptance and owner decision
+
+S4-02c remains **accepted with carries**. Its transactional enqueue, scoped drain, one-shot run plan and two-leg authored demonstration satisfy its packet. F1 is upstream S3/S4 semantics and a new S5 eligibility requirement; R1 is unscheduled upstream operations. The reviewer explicitly did not make either an S4-02c acceptance gap. Close `I-evidence-acceptance-consequence-work` on merge after the review's documentation carries; leave the two new nodes open.
+
+**Owner input:** No additional product choice is needed to make these safety and lineage rulings. The owner should see the no-amount state and limited Finding at the existing S5-01 visual checkpoint, and decide any broader analysis-input policy at the W1-exit review. If the owner wants partial, explicitly limited money from an indeterminate generator series, that would be a new product/risk decision with a separate reviewed contract; it is not implied by the current S5 eligibility rule.
+
+## Draft DECISIONS entry
+
+Decision: `D-2026-10-14-s402c-late-sequence-and-s5-money`. The Architect rules that gateway admission sequence does not establish source-time order for a validated store-and-forward source. S3 must version a source-time-aware cohort rule with explicit clock/overlap/epoch limits and reassess affected windows without rewriting history. S4 must carry a material series refusal into the revised Finding and state why the episode ends. Until a reviewed reassessment resolves generator-series ambiguity, S5 withholds an amount for that affected selected Finding/window despite a `CURRENT PRICED` consequence, and shows the limitation and exact lineage. `I-late-reading-series-and-money-limit` and `I-analytic-finding-worker-schedule` are separate prerequisites of `I-site-overview-read` before S5-01; both also gate real-Site readiness. The latter schedules S3/S4 workers and makes backlog/failure visible so late evidence reaches the revised Finding without manual commands. The broader simulated/real analysis-input backlog remains for W1 exit. S4-02c acceptance is unchanged; its reviewed consequence work may close on merge. The S5 owner visual checkpoint remains required.
+
+## Plain-language owner summary
+
+The gateway numbers a delayed reading when it arrives. Today that can make the analysis stop early and show **$7.5625 as current** where the same readings numbered in their source order yield **$15.8125**, without saying the series was cut short. I have gated the S5 money card until the reading order is handled under a reviewed rule and the Finding explains any remaining limit. I also added a small scheduling gate so delayed evidence reaches the revised analysis and Finding automatically. This does not reopen S4-02c's acceptance.

# Architect rulings: S4-02c review F1 Q1â€“Q3 and R1 (2026-10-14)

Inputs: `.agent/S4-02c-review.md` F1 and registry closeout notes, `.agent/S4-02c-review-packet.md`, `.agent/S4-02c-walkthrough-evidence.md` run 1, `tasks/S4-02c-evidence-consequence-work.md` R1; `D-2026-10-09-s2-simulated-publication-clock`, the S3 dispatch decisions, `D-2026-10-14-s402-post-review-follow-ons`, and `D-2026-10-14-s5-selected-window-overview`. This is a ruling for subsequent work, not a change to S4-02c's reviewed contract.

## Q1 â€” sequence and source time

**Rule:** An admission-allocated gateway sequence is transport/admission order, not proof of source-time order. For a registered same-source, same-epoch stream whose source-time/interval semantics and clock quality are attested and valid, S3 must place readings by source time. A later gateway sequence with an earlier source time is a late arrival, not `SEQUENCE_ORDER_INVERTED` by itself. Preserve duplicate, overlap, conflicting epoch, untrusted clock, and impossible-time refusals; where the source-time basis cannot be established, report a named series limit rather than silently sort and claim coherence. This does not bless arbitrary backdating. The Lab-delayed publication clock supplies a deterministic case: the withheld report has no sequence before release, so admission numbering naturally runs backward against source time.

+# Architect rulings: S4-02c review F1 Q1–Q3 and R1 (2026-10-14)
+
+Inputs: `.agent/S4-02c-review.md` F1 and registry closeout notes, `.agent/S4-02c-review-packet.md`, `.agent/S4-02c-walkthrough-evidence.md` run 1, `tasks/S4-02c-evidence-consequence-work.md` R1; `D-2026-10-09-s2-simulated-publication-clock`, the S3 dispatch decisions, `D-2026-10-14-s402-post-review-follow-ons`, and `D-2026-10-14-s5-selected-window-overview`. This is a ruling for subsequent work, not a change to S4-02c's reviewed contract.
+
+## Q1 — sequence and source time
+
+**Rule:** An admission-allocated gateway sequence is transport/admission order, not proof of source-time order. For a registered same-source, same-epoch stream whose source-time/interval semantics and clock quality are attested and valid, S3 must place readings by source time. A later gateway sequence with an earlier source time is a late arrival, not `SEQUENCE_ORDER_INVERTED` by itself. Preserve duplicate, overlap, conflicting epoch, untrusted clock, and impossible-time refusals; where the source-time basis cannot be established, report a named series limit rather than silently sort and claim coherence. This does not bless arbitrary backdating. The Lab-delayed publication clock supplies a deterministic case: the withheld report has no sequence before release, so admission numbering naturally runs backward against source time.
+
+**Owner and timing:** S3 cohort/assessment (`dispatch-3.x`) plus S2 gateway/publication-profile proof, in `I-late-reading-series-and-money-limit`, **before S5-01's money read and before a real-Site pilot**. Changing the reviewed cohort rule requires a new model version, reassessment/reconciliation of affected current windows and preservation of old `dispatch-3.1` revisions and exact links as history. The implementer must prove both on-time-sequenced late upload and admission-sequenced delayed admission through accepted public evidence. A real gateway without validated source-time/clock semantics stays limited.
+
+## Q2 — Finding limit and money
+
+**Rule:** A revised Finding must carry the selected assessment's material `GENERATOR_SERIES_AMBIGUOUS`/`SEQUENCE_ORDER_INVERTED` limit when it removes or truncates the prior candidate episode. Its end reason must identify the series refusal; `OPEN_BOUND` alone is false for the run-1 truncation. Preserve the supported `[06:05, 07:00)` portion if its exact evidence remains coherent, but disclose that the later portion is unassessed, not disproved or repaired. S4 owns FindingRevision propagation and its read/UI; a changed claim basis appends a revision.
+
+S5's `mini:4#a` money read **withholds the amount** if generator-series ambiguity affects the selected Finding/window, even if a narrower consequence is `CURRENT PRICED`. Show an explicit no-current-amount state with the assessment/Finding limit and exact links. This is a fail-closed rule for the demonstrated silent understatement, not a claim that every `INDETERMINATE` window has no valid candidate time. Once S3 resolves and reassesses that series under a reviewed rule, S5 may show a same-basis current amount for the proven Candidate span, with any remaining material limits visible. S4 consequence currentness remains a statement about the cited FindingRevision's technical/price basis; S5 eligibility is a stricter presentation gate. Do not rewrite historical $7.5625 or $15.8125 consequences.
+
+**Owner and timing:** S4 Finding projection and S5 `I-site-overview-read`/UI consume the S3 decision in `I-late-reading-series-and-money-limit`; **before S5-01**. The real-Site pilot also needs the source-time/clock proof. A regression must replay run 1 and the source-ordered variant and assert the assessment status, Finding limitations/end reason, consequence lineage and S5 amount eligibility; the 7.5625 USD current consequence must never become an unqualified current Overview amount.
+
+## Q3 — placement and gates
+
+**Rule:** F1 gets its own sized node, `I-late-reading-series-and-money-limit` (**M**), because it changes reviewed S3 assessment semantics, S4 claim semantics and S5 money eligibility. It is a hard prerequisite of `I-site-overview-read`, hence S5-01, with `I-S2-02`, `I-S3-01`, `I-S4-01`, `I-S4-02b` as inputs. The node's acceptance target records both late-numbering variants and the no-silent-money result. It also gates the first real-Site pilot. The owner's “analysis input data for simulated and real Sites” backlog item remains the broader W1-exit contract for per-analytic required inputs, cadence and coverage; it should include source-time/clock attestation at that review, but does not substitute for this narrower S5 defect gate. R1 concerns operating the already defined jobs and is separate from semantic correctness.
+
+## R1 — run the S3 and S4 workers
+
+**Rule:** Create `I-analytic-finding-worker-schedule` (**S**), requiring S3, S4 and S4-02c's consequence-work node, and gate `I-site-overview-read` on it. Install or explicitly configure an environment-owned bounded schedule for `process-jobs` then `match-findings` across active tenant/Sites; report backlog, last success/failure, retry and stopped-worker conditions. Keep S5 `PENDING`/`STALE_PROJECTION` while upstream work is outstanding. A late accepted reading must reach a revised Finding and consequence without the manual Leg B commands. The S4-02c one-shot consequence runner and its documented external timer do not schedule S3/S4.
+
+**Owner and timing:** S3/S4 worker operation, with S5 currentness integration; **before S5-01**, and therefore before W1 exit or a real-Site pilot that claims automatic late-evidence recovery. The Planner should refine deployment ownership and cadence in a small follow-on packet. No new scheduler mechanism is mandated if an existing reliable environment timer can meet the acceptance target.
+
+## Acceptance and owner decision
+
+S4-02c remains **accepted with carries**. Its transactional enqueue, scoped drain, one-shot run plan and two-leg authored demonstration satisfy its packet. F1 is upstream S3/S4 semantics and a new S5 eligibility requirement; R1 is unscheduled upstream operations. The reviewer explicitly did not make either an S4-02c acceptance gap. Close `I-evidence-acceptance-consequence-work` on merge after the review's documentation carries; leave the two new nodes open.
+
+**Owner input:** No additional product choice is needed to make these safety and lineage rulings. The owner should see the no-amount state and limited Finding at the existing S5-01 visual checkpoint, and decide any broader analysis-input policy at the W1-exit review. If the owner wants partial, explicitly limited money from an indeterminate generator series, that would be a new product/risk decision with a separate reviewed contract; it is not implied by the current S5 eligibility rule.
+
+## Draft DECISIONS entry
+
+Decision: `D-2026-10-14-s402c-late-sequence-and-s5-money`. The Architect rules that gateway admission sequence does not establish source-time order for a validated store-and-forward source. S3 must version a source-time-aware cohort rule with explicit clock/overlap/epoch limits and reassess affected windows without rewriting history. S4 must carry a material series refusal into the revised Finding and state why the episode ends. Until a reviewed reassessment resolves generator-series ambiguity, S5 withholds an amount for that affected selected Finding/window despite a `CURRENT PRICED` consequence, and shows the limitation and exact lineage. `I-late-reading-series-and-money-limit` and `I-analytic-finding-worker-schedule` are separate prerequisites of `I-site-overview-read` before S5-01; both also gate real-Site readiness. The latter schedules S3/S4 workers and makes backlog/failure visible so late evidence reaches the revised Finding without manual commands. The broader simulated/real analysis-input backlog remains for W1 exit. S4-02c acceptance is unchanged; its reviewed consequence work may close on merge. The S5 owner visual checkpoint remains required.
+
+## Plain-language owner summary
+
+The gateway numbers a delayed reading when it arrives. Today that can make the analysis stop early and show **$7.5625 as current** where the same readings numbered in their source order yield **$15.8125**, without saying the series was cut short. I have gated the S5 money card until the reading order is handled under a reviewed rule and the Finding explains any remaining limit. I also added a small scheduling gate so delayed evidence reaches the revised analysis and Finding automatically. This does not reopen S4-02c's acceptance.

+# Architect rulings: S4-02c review F1 Q1–Q3 and R1 (2026-10-14)
+
+Inputs: `.agent/S4-02c-review.md` F1 and registry closeout notes, `.agent/S4-02c-review-packet.md`, `.agent/S4-02c-walkthrough-evidence.md` run 1, `tasks/S4-02c-evidence-consequence-work.md` R1; `D-2026-10-09-s2-simulated-publication-clock`, the S3 dispatch decisions, `D-2026-10-14-s402-post-review-follow-ons`, and `D-2026-10-14-s5-selected-window-overview`. This is a ruling for subsequent work, not a change to S4-02c's reviewed contract.
+
+## Q1 — sequence and source time
+
+**Rule:** An admission-allocated gateway sequence is transport/admission order, not proof of source-time order. For a registered same-source, same-epoch stream whose source-time/interval semantics and clock quality are attested and valid, S3 must place readings by source time. A later gateway sequence with an earlier source time is a late arrival, not `SEQUENCE_ORDER_INVERTED` by itself. Preserve duplicate, overlap, conflicting epoch, untrusted clock, and impossible-time refusals; where the source-time basis cannot be established, report a named series limit rather than silently sort and claim coherence. This does not bless arbitrary backdating. The Lab-delayed publication clock supplies a deterministic case: the withheld report has no sequence before release, so admission numbering naturally runs backward against source time.
+
+**Owner and timing:** S3 cohort/assessment (`dispatch-3.x`) plus S2 gateway/publication-profile proof, in `I-late-reading-series-and-money-limit`, **before S5-01's money read and before a real-Site pilot**. Changing the reviewed cohort rule requires a new model version, reassessment/reconciliation of affected current windows and preservation of old `dispatch-3.1` revisions and exact links as history. The implementer must prove both on-time-sequenced late upload and admission-sequenced delayed admission through accepted public evidence. A real gateway without validated source-time/clock semantics stays limited.
+
+## Q2 — Finding limit and money
+
+**Rule:** A revised Finding must carry the selected assessment's material `GENERATOR_SERIES_AMBIGUOUS`/`SEQUENCE_ORDER_INVERTED` limit when it removes or truncates the prior candidate episode. Its end reason must identify the series refusal; `OPEN_BOUND` alone is false for the run-1 truncation. Preserve the supported `[06:05, 07:00)` portion if its exact evidence remains coherent, but disclose that the later portion is unassessed, not disproved or repaired. S4 owns FindingRevision propagation and its read/UI; a changed claim basis appends a revision.
+
+S5's `mini:4#a` money read **withholds the amount** if generator-series ambiguity affects the selected Finding/window, even if a narrower consequence is `CURRENT PRICED`. Show an explicit no-current-amount state with the assessment/Finding limit and exact links. This is a fail-closed rule for the demonstrated silent understatement, not a claim that every `INDETERMINATE` window has no valid candidate time. Once S3 resolves and reassesses that series under a reviewed rule, S5 may show a same-basis current amount for the proven Candidate span, with any remaining material limits visible. S4 consequence currentness remains a statement about the cited FindingRevision's technical/price basis; S5 eligibility is a stricter presentation gate. Do not rewrite historical $7.5625 or $15.8125 consequences.
+
+**Owner and timing:** S4 Finding projection and S5 `I-site-overview-read`/UI consume the S3 decision in `I-late-reading-series-and-money-limit`; **before S5-01**. The real-Site pilot also needs the source-time/clock proof. A regression must replay run 1 and the source-ordered variant and assert the assessment status, Finding limitations/end reason, consequence lineage and S5 amount eligibility; the 7.5625 USD current consequence must never become an unqualified current Overview amount.
+
+## Q3 — placement and gates
+
+**Rule:** F1 gets its own sized node, `I-late-reading-series-and-money-limit` (**M**), because it changes reviewed S3 assessment semantics, S4 claim semantics and S5 money eligibility. It is a hard prerequisite of `I-site-overview-read`, hence S5-01, with `I-S2-02`, `I-S3-01`, `I-S4-01`, `I-S4-02b` as inputs. The node's acceptance target records both late-numbering variants and the no-silent-money result. It also gates the first real-Site pilot. The owner's “analysis input data for simulated and real Sites” backlog item remains the broader W1-exit contract for per-analytic required inputs, cadence and coverage; it should include source-time/clock attestation at that review, but does not substitute for this narrower S5 defect gate. R1 concerns operating the already defined jobs and is separate from semantic correctness.
+
+## R1 — run the S3 and S4 workers
+
+**Rule:** Create `I-analytic-finding-worker-schedule` (**S**), requiring S3, S4 and S4-02c's consequence-work node, and gate `I-site-overview-read` on it. Install or explicitly configure an environment-owned bounded schedule for `process-jobs` then `match-findings` across active tenant/Sites; report backlog, last success/failure, retry and stopped-worker conditions. Keep S5 `PENDING`/`STALE_PROJECTION` while upstream work is outstanding. A late accepted reading must reach a revised Finding and consequence without the manual Leg B commands. The S4-02c one-shot consequence runner and its documented external timer do not schedule S3/S4.
+
+**Owner and timing:** S3/S4 worker operation, with S5 currentness integration; **before S5-01**, and therefore before W1 exit or a real-Site pilot that claims automatic late-evidence recovery. The Planner should refine deployment ownership and cadence in a small follow-on packet. No new scheduler mechanism is mandated if an existing reliable environment timer can meet the acceptance target.
+
+## Acceptance and owner decision
+
+S4-02c remains **accepted with carries**. Its transactional enqueue, scoped drain, one-shot run plan and two-leg authored demonstration satisfy its packet. F1 is upstream S3/S4 semantics and a new S5 eligibility requirement; R1 is unscheduled upstream operations. The reviewer explicitly did not make either an S4-02c acceptance gap. Close `I-evidence-acceptance-consequence-work` on merge after the review's documentation carries; leave the two new nodes open.
+
+**Owner input:** No additional product choice is needed to make these safety and lineage rulings. The owner should see the no-amount state and limited Finding at the existing S5-01 visual checkpoint, and decide any broader analysis-input policy at the W1-exit review. If the owner wants partial, explicitly limited money from an indeterminate generator series, that would be a new product/risk decision with a separate reviewed contract; it is not implied by the current S5 eligibility rule.
+
+## Draft DECISIONS entry
+
+Decision: `D-2026-10-14-s402c-late-sequence-and-s5-money`. The Architect rules that gateway admission sequence does not establish source-time order for a validated store-and-forward source. S3 must version a source-time-aware cohort rule with explicit clock/overlap/epoch limits and reassess affected windows without rewriting history. S4 must carry a material series refusal into the revised Finding and state why the episode ends. Until a reviewed reassessment resolves generator-series ambiguity, S5 withholds an amount for that affected selected Finding/window despite a `CURRENT PRICED` consequence, and shows the limitation and exact lineage. `I-late-reading-series-and-money-limit` and `I-analytic-finding-worker-schedule` are separate prerequisites of `I-site-overview-read` before S5-01; both also gate real-Site readiness. The latter schedules S3/S4 workers and makes backlog/failure visible so late evidence reaches the revised Finding without manual commands. The broader simulated/real analysis-input backlog remains for W1 exit. S4-02c acceptance is unchanged; its reviewed consequence work may close on merge. The S5 owner visual checkpoint remains required.
+
+## Plain-language owner summary
+
+The gateway numbers a delayed reading when it arrives. Today that can make the analysis stop early and show **$7.5625 as current** where the same readings numbered in their source order yield **$15.8125**, without saying the series was cut short. I have gated the S5 money card until the reading order is handled under a reviewed rule and the Finding explains any remaining limit. I also added a small scheduling gate so delayed evidence reaches the revised analysis and Finding automatically. This does not reopen S4-02c's acceptance.

The S5 owner visual checkpoint remains required.
+

+
+The gateway numbers a delayed reading when it arrives. I have gated the S5 money card until the reading order is handled under a reviewed rule and the Finding explains any remaining limit. I also added a small scheduling gate so delayed evidence reaches the revised analysis and Finding automatically. This does not reopen S4-02c's acceptance.

+# Architect rulings: S4-02c review F1 Q1–Q3 and R1 (2026-10-14)
+
+Inputs: `.agent/S4-02c-review.md` F1 and registry closeout notes, `.agent/S4-02c-review-packet.md`, `.agent/S4-02c-walkthrough-evidence.md` run 1, `tasks/S4-02c-evidence-consequence-work.md` R1; `D-2026-10-09-s2-simulated-publication-clock`, the S3 dispatch decisions, `D-2026-10-14-s402-post-review-follow-ons`, and `D-2026-10-14-s5-selected-window-overview`. This is a ruling for subsequent work, not a change to S4-02c's reviewed contract.
+
+## Q1 — sequence and source time
+
+**Rule:** An admission-allocated gateway sequence is transport/admission order, not proof of source-time order. For a registered same-source, same-epoch stream whose source-time/interval semantics and clock quality are attested and valid, S3 must place readings by source time. A later gateway sequence with an earlier source time is a late arrival, not `SEQUENCE_ORDER_INVERTED` by itself. Preserve duplicate, overlap, conflicting epoch, untrusted clock, and impossible-time refusals; where the source-time basis cannot be established, report a named series limit rather than silently sort and claim coherence. This does not bless arbitrary backdating. The Lab-delayed publication clock supplies a deterministic case: the withheld report has no sequence before release, so admission numbering naturally runs backward against source time.
+
+**Owner and timing:** S3 cohort/assessment (`dispatch-3.x`) plus S2 gateway/publication-profile proof, in `I-late-reading-series-and-money-limit`, **before S5-01's money read and before a real-Site pilot**. Changing the reviewed cohort rule requires a new model version, reassessment/reconciliation of affected current windows and preservation of old `dispatch-3.1` revisions and exact links as history. The implementer must prove both on-time-sequenced late upload and admission-sequenced delayed admission through accepted public evidence. A real gateway without validated source-time/clock semantics stays limited.
+
+## Q2 — Finding limit and money
+
+**Rule:** A revised Finding must carry the selected assessment's material `GENERATOR_SERIES_AMBIGUOUS`/`SEQUENCE_ORDER_INVERTED` limit when it removes or truncates the prior candidate episode. Its end reason must identify the series refusal; `OPEN_BOUND` alone is false for the run-1 truncation. Preserve the supported `[06:05, 07:00)` portion if its exact evidence remains coherent, but disclose that the later portion is unassessed, not disproved or repaired. S4 owns FindingRevision propagation and its read/UI; a changed claim basis appends a revision.
+
+S5's `mini:4#a` money read **withholds the amount** if generator-series ambiguity affects the selected Finding/window, even if a narrower consequence is `CURRENT PRICED`. Show an explicit no-current-amount state with the assessment/Finding limit and exact links. This is a fail-closed rule for the demonstrated silent understatement, not a claim that every `INDETERMINATE` window has no valid candidate time. Once S3 resolves and reassesses that series under a reviewed rule, S5 may show a same-basis current amount for the proven Candidate span, with any remaining material limits visible. S4 consequence currentness remains a statement about the cited FindingRevision's technical/price basis; S5 eligibility is a stricter presentation gate. Do not rewrite historical $7.5625 or $15.8125 consequences.
+
+**Owner and timing:** S4 Finding projection and S5 `I-site-overview-read`/UI consume the S3 decision in `I-late-reading-series-and-money-limit`; **before S5-01**. The real-Site pilot also needs the source-time/clock proof. A regression must replay run 1 and the source-ordered variant and assert the assessment status, Finding limitations/end reason, consequence lineage and S5 amount eligibility; the 7.5625 USD current consequence must never become an unqualified current Overview amount.
+
+## Q3 — placement and gates
+
+**Rule:** F1 gets its own sized node, `I-late-reading-series-and-money-limit` (**M**), because it changes reviewed S3 assessment semantics, S4 claim semantics and S5 money eligibility. It is a hard prerequisite of `I-site-overview-read`, hence S5-01, with `I-S2-02`, `I-S3-01`, `I-S4-01`, `I-S4-02b` as inputs. The node's acceptance target records both late-numbering variants and the no-silent-money result. It also gates the first real-Site pilot. The owner's “analysis input data for simulated and real Sites” backlog item remains the broader W1-exit contract for per-analytic required inputs, cadence and coverage; it should include source-time/clock attestation at that review, but does not substitute for this narrower S5 defect gate. R1 concerns operating the already defined jobs and is separate from semantic correctness.
+
+## R1 — run the S3 and S4 workers
+
+**Rule:** Create `I-analytic-finding-worker-schedule` (**S**), requiring S3, S4 and S4-02c's consequence-work node, and gate `I-site-overview-read` on it. Install or explicitly configure an environment-owned bounded schedule for `process-jobs` then `match-findings` across active tenant/Sites; report backlog, last success/failure, retry and stopped-worker conditions. Keep S5 `PENDING`/`STALE_PROJECTION` while upstream work is outstanding. A late accepted reading must reach a revised Finding and consequence without the manual Leg B commands. The S4-02c one-shot consequence runner and its documented external timer do not schedule S3/S4.
+
+**Owner and timing:** S3/S4 worker operation, with S5 currentness integration; **before S5-01**, and therefore before W1 exit or a real-Site pilot that claims automatic late-evidence recovery. The Planner should refine deployment ownership and cadence in a small follow-on packet. No new scheduler mechanism is mandated if an existing reliable environment timer can meet the acceptance target.
+
+## Acceptance and owner decision
+
+S4-02c remains **accepted with carries**. Its transactional enqueue, scoped drain, one-shot run plan and two-leg authored demonstration satisfy its packet. F1 is upstream S3/S4 semantics and a new S5 eligibility requirement; R1 is unscheduled upstream operations. The reviewer explicitly did not make either an S4-02c acceptance gap. Close `I-evidence-acceptance-consequence-work` on merge after the review's documentation carries; leave the two new nodes open.
+
+**Owner input:** No additional product choice is needed to make these safety and lineage rulings. The owner should see the no-amount state and limited Finding at the existing S5-01 visual checkpoint, and decide any broader analysis-input policy at the W1-exit review. If the owner wants partial, explicitly limited money from an indeterminate generator series, that would be a new product/risk decision with a separate reviewed contract; it is not implied by the current S5 eligibility rule.
+
+## Draft DECISIONS entry
+
+Decision: `D-2026-10-14-s402c-late-sequence-and-s5-money`. The Architect rules that gateway admission sequence does not establish source-time order for a validated store-and-forward source. S3 must version a source-time-aware cohort rule with explicit clock/overlap/epoch limits and reassess affected windows without rewriting history. S4 must carry a material series refusal into the revised Finding and state why the episode ends. Until a reviewed reassessment resolves generator-series ambiguity, S5 withholds an amount for that affected selected Finding/window despite a `CURRENT PRICED` consequence, and shows the limitation and exact lineage. `I-late-reading-series-and-money-limit` and `I-analytic-finding-worker-schedule` are separate prerequisites of `I-site-overview-read` before S5-01; both also gate real-Site readiness. The latter schedules S3/S4 workers and makes backlog/failure visible so late evidence reaches the revised Finding without manual commands. The broader simulated/real analysis-input backlog remains for W1 exit. S4-02c acceptance is unchanged; its reviewed consequence work may close on merge. The S5 owner visual checkpoint remains required.
+
+## Plain-language owner summary
+
+The gateway numbers a delayed reading when it arrives. Today that can make the analysis stop early and show **$7.5625 as current** where the same readings numbered in their source order yield **$15.8125**, without saying the series was cut short. I have gated the S5 money card until the reading order is handled under a reviewed rule and the Finding explains any remaining limit. I also added a small scheduling gate so delayed evidence reaches the revised analysis and Finding automatically. This does not reopen S4-02c's acceptance.
